title: Residency-aware routing + evacuation delay controls for Private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Add a deterministic, auditable mechanism for Private/VPC deployments to control regional failover behavior and residency enforcement while preserving operational reliability. This ticket designs and implements a residency-aware routing layer with an evacuation delay (grace period) and evidence/reporting hooks so customers can configure retention/residency constraints and receive verifiable audit artifacts when cross-region fallback occurs. Scope covers control-plane policy, data-plane routing changes, audit log schema, and rollout strategy for existing Private clusters.
background: Customers in regulated regions require both strict residency and a predictable path for graceful degradation during regional outages. Current behavior falls back immediately to the nearest region which lacks an auditable holdback and retention-aware egress control. We need a controlled evacuation flow: (1) attempt local processing, (2) if capacity/health degraded, apply a configurable evacuation-delay timer that keeps requests pinned while autoscaling and routing converge, (3) after the timer expires, failover to approved regional replicas with explicit audit evidence and sanitized retention markers.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can configure per-tenant residency policy (allowed regions list, strict/residency-first flag) in the Private Console
A new routing layer honors residency policy and enforces an evacuation-delay timer before cross-region routing is allowed
When failover occurs, an evidence bundle is generated (request ids, timestamps, chosen fallback region, retention_policy_applied) and stored in the audit pipeline
Audit evidence is queryable via Console and exposed as an S3-compatible archive for customers and compliance teams
Retention markers travel with the request metadata so destination region enforces the originating tenant's retention obligations
E2E tests cover normal, partial outage, cold-start scaling, and forced-evacuation scenarios with reproducible logs
Rollout plan that allows feature gating by tenant and a global kill-switch
No regression to latency p50/p99 SLAs outside of controlled degraded windows (documented in rollout notes)
tasks: Design control-plane API for residency policy and evacuation delay (config schema and validation)
Implement routing middleware that consults residency policy and maintains per-request timer state
Add retention metadata propagation hooks to the data-plane proxy layer
Add audit evidence aggregator and S3 archival step with tamper-evident metadata
Create Console UI to show pending evacuations, recent failovers, and export evidence bundles
Integrate with KMS for evidence encryption and HSM-backed signing options
Author unit/integration tests and a chaos test harness scenario
Prepare rollout playbook, migration plan, and customer communication templates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Evacuation-delay increases p99 latency during partial outages. Mitigation: make timer configurable per-tenant with adaptive short-circuit if health metrics degrade beyond threshold.
Risk: Evidence bundle could include sensitive data. Mitigation: sanitize sensitive fields and require KMS encryption for stored artifacts.
Risk: Incorrect retention propagation causing unlawful data movement. Mitigation: add strict validation and a preflight verification step before allowing cross-region writes.

Risk: Complexity in state management across fleet. Mitigation: keep per-request timer state in ephemeral control-plane cache with bounded TTL and fall back to stateless decision path if cache unavailable.
Risk: Too many customers enable strict residency causing capacity hotspots. Mitigation: provide autoscaling guidance, backpressure signals, and hard limits per-tenant with recommended burst policies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy parsing and validation rules
Integration tests that simulate regional outage and verify evacuation-delay behavior
Chaos experiments that kill regional control-plane nodes and validate failover/evidence generation
Performance benchmarks to measure p50/p99 delta with evacuation-delay enabled across common payloads
Compliance test suite that verifies evidence bundle contains required fields and is encrypted
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind tenant opt-in in the Console
Enable for internal 'Redwood-SIM' tenants and run against staging for 2 weeks
Beta with 3 pilot customers in EU and APAC with legal approval
Gradual ramp to all Private tenants with monitoring and automatic rollback thresholds
Post-rollout audit: run retention/evidence queries for pilot tenants and produce compliance report

notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: residency-first tenants will see stronger restrictions and longer evacuation delays by default. The engineering trade-off is between strict compliance and latency; shipping with tenant-level knobs and strong audit evidence keeps us aligned with enterprise requirements.
